title: What If the Great Salt Lake Dried Up Completely?

scenes.text: What if the Great Salt Lake dried up? The danger isn't the water, it's the dust.
By 2022, about 800 square miles of lakebed were already exposed, roughly the size of Maui.
Wind lifts dust from that dry bed, and only about 9 percent of it was actively producing dust.
The dust contains metals, and arsenic is the highest compared with EPA standards.
About 2.5 million people live downwind along the Wasatch Front.
California spent over 2 billion dollars on dust control at Owens Lake. Utah would face the same fight.
